turns.player: Walk quietly and let the road speak — use Tremor Sense to read what moves on the hillside tonight
turns.summary: Adelheid walked the moonlit sluice-road, Tremor Sense confirming the Precursor pulse runs steadily beneath this ground too — south-southeast, unwavering, persistent.
turns.narration:
The sluice-road climbs in good stone — old-cut steps worn smooth in the middle, wild thyme pressing into the cracks. Moonlight comes down clean. Vreni walks a half-step ahead, her habit pale as birch bark, her sandals nearly silent.

You let your weight settle into each step and open the craft low, the way you'd lean an ear to a wall to hear the room beyond it. Tremor Sense reaches out into the hillside — not a push, just a receiving. What comes back: the slow, regular press of two deer moving through the coppice a hundred paces widdershins, the faint churn of water in the irrigation channel that runs alongside the road, the tiny percussion of mice in the terrace wall. The hill is ordinary and alive and unthreatened.

One thing is not ordinary. Running beneath the road, south-southeast the way the roots run, is the deep pulse — slower than a heartbeat, more patient than stone — the same Precursor vibration that hummed beneath the terrace. It is quieter here, farther from its surface expressions, but it is continuous and steady and absolutely present. It does not quicken when you listen. It simply persists, the way a river persists.

Aevi drifts close to your ear, her motes just bright enough to read. "Still same direction," she says, very quietly. "It runs under this road too." She dims back to near-nothing. Sister Vreni glances at the teal flicker but does not ask — a woman who has walked these hills long enough to know that some travelers carry things you do not inquire after, at night, on a steep road.

turns.player: Stop to listen more carefully where the road crosses a runnel — press both hands to the stone and read the pulse beneath it with Echo Sense
turns.summary: On the sluice-road above Millbrook, Adelheid pressed her hands to the stone at a drainage runnel and confirmed with Echo Sense that the Precursor pulse runs directly beneath the road — Aevi began unconsciously matching its rhythm.
turns.narration:
A thin runnel cuts across the road where the upper terrace drains — just wide enough to step over, the stone around it darker and cold. You pause there, crouch, and press both palms flat to the step.

Echo Sense opens outward through the rock — not through air, through stone — and what comes back is layered. The runnel itself, tracing a shallow path under the step and out through a weep-hole in the terrace wall. The deeper water of the irrigation channel, heavier and slower, running alongside the road a pace to your left. And beneath all of it, beneath the foundation cuts and the packed earth and the old mortar, the pulse. The same one you touched in the terrace two days ago. It runs here too, south-southeast, steady as a heartbeat that has never once faltered. Stronger than you expected — not because it has grown, but because the road sits directly over its line. The stone carries it faithfully.

Aevi drifts down from your shoulder and hovers just above the runnel, her motes dimming until they are almost gone — then brightening in a slow, regular rhythm. Once. Pause. Once. Pause. She is matching the pulse. She does not do it deliberately, you think; she does it the way a person hums to something they half-remember.

Vreni has stopped two steps ahead. She is looking back at you, unhurried, her hands folded into her sleeves. She does not ask what you are doing. She simply waits, with the particular patience of someone who has learned to let a healer work.

echo-river-contamination.label: Echo River Contamination
facts: [d1] The Echo River runs with a gray-green iridescence on the surface, visible at Millbrook's dock on Day 1 morning. Fish catches are thin. Villagers draw from the well rather than the river without saying…

[d1] Echo Sense reveals fish are actively avoiding the shallows near Millbrook's dock, clustering in deep cold water on the far bank. The riverbed beneath the dock is unnaturally flat and dense — not consi…

[d1] The river runs gray-green at the dock and at the tree-line visible from the Wet Meadows. The Wet Meadows are impassable in early spring due to melt runoff and standing water—direct approach to the river from the terrace side is blocked until the water subsides.

[d2] Edvar Crane's three-week reading has tracked the contamination's deepening from edge-staining to full saturation. The water is not passively contaminated—something beneath it is actively waking and causing the spread. The phenomenon is ongoing and accelerating.

[d2] The contamination's timeline matches Silas Weir's presence at the sluice-turn three weeks ago. He was listening to something in the water with tuning instruments. The sequence suggests cause and consequence rather than random poisoning—whatever Silas heard may have triggered what is now waking.

[d2] The direct path to the sluice-turn (where Silas was last seen three weeks ago) lies through the Wet Meadows, which are impassable during spring melt. The higher route climbs through the terrace gardens and old stone-cuts, skirting the flood but adding significant time to the journey.

[d2] The wayhouse above the pass road sits on the sluice-road and would have seen any travelers heading upstream — including anyone who passed through three weeks ago toward the sluice-turn where Silas Weir was last seen.

Adelheid's attempt to meditate into resonance with it caused…

It is not randomly waking; it is executing a directive. The question is not what woke it but what it does when it finishes waking…

[d2] A reclamation system beneath Millbrook is not newly waking—it is actively executing a directive, continuously executing, and has been executing since before Adelheid touched it. It is not a dormant relic awakening; it is infrastructure that never stopped working and is now entering a more active…

[d2] The Precursor system beneath Millbrook runs south-southeast toward the sluice-turn where Silas Weir was listening three weeks ago. The system may have been broadcasting a signal detectable by a trained Harmonic ear — Silas arrived with a receiver, not a transmitter.

It maintains the same south-southeast direction and does not respond to being listened to. The signal's reach extends further than the surface plant-expressions suggested.

[d2] The Precursor pulse runs directly beneath the sluice-road above Millbrook — not only under the terrace and Wet Meadows but along the road itself, which sits over its south-southeast line. Echo Sense through stone confirms it, steady and unfailing. The road may follow the signal, or be built over…

personalArc.name: The Root Remembers
personalArc.premise: A Swiss herbalist transplanted to an alien soil carries a silver-stemmed cutting from her village — the last living thread to everything she understood — and must decide whether her knowledge is a heritage to preserve or a seed to break open and replant entirely, in ground that does not know her name.
personalArc.stakes: To remain the keeper of a dead village's remedies, or to become something that village never imagined: a healer fluent in two earths, whose hands hold the old world and the new one at once — or to lose both trying.

legendNpc.name: The Silver-Stemmed Cutting
legendNpc.role: the last living root of her Swiss village, wrapped in linen and slowly dying, the mute accusation of every mile she was

stages.objective: the cutting that will not root — she has tried three times; the Korean soil rejects it, or she does not yet know how to ask; Mara Wells has seen this particular grief before, in other hands, and says so plainly

the remedy that should not work — she compounds a draught from Korean plants she only half-understands, borrowing Piotr's hard-won field notes, and it heals something her Swiss formulary swore was untreatable; the success feels like a betrayal, and a door

the linen unwrapped — the cutting is failing; she must choose what she owes it, what she owes Millbrook, and what she owes the healer she is becoming; the answer is in what she does with the roots when she finally opens the wrapping and faces what is left

personalArc.notes_for_gm: A generated PERSONAL arc (SNG-133) — surface it as a slow gravity across sessions; the ending is the player's, never foreclosed.
